components.css: .ds-login-card { position: relative; overflow: hidden; width: 360px; padding: 40px 40px 32px; border-radius: 20px; background: #fff; color: #0b1b3f; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(2, 10, 40, 0.3), 0 30px 70px rgba(2, 10, 40, 0.45); } .ds-login-progress { position: absolute; inset: 0 0 auto; height: 4px; overflow: hidden; background: #e4eaf5; } .ds-login-progress::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; width: 42%; border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #e02a2a, #e8742a 55%, #e1b115); animation: ds-login-sweep 1.1s cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) infinite; } .ds-login-title { margin: 0; font: 800 27px/1.2 Montserrat, Roboto, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: #051f63; } .ds-login-sub { margin: 8px 0 0; font: 400 14.5px/1.45 Roboto, sans-serif; color: #46557a; } @keyframes ds-login-sweep { from { transform: translateX(-100%); } to { transform: translateX(240%); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-login-progress::after { width: 100%; border-radius: 0; animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
A tidy, well-lit registration counter. Everything is labelled, status is visible at a glance, and the tone is friendly but businesslike. White cards sit on a pale blue-grey page under a navy header that lifts to PAL blue; the header and the filled buttons carry the colour, and the working surfaces stay white.

The feel is soft and friendly: pill buttons, generously rounded cards, light layered shadows and heavy headings. It is built on Angular Material 3 (light scheme only, density 0) with global overrides in `frontend/web/src/styles.scss`, so every Material component picks up the same shapes and colours.
keyCharacteristics: White cards on a pale blue-grey page, gradient header on top.
Blue carries action; green, amber and red carry status.
Pill buttons and pills for status; rounded rectangles for everything that holds content.
Bold headings (700 to 800) over regular 14px body text.
Light scheme only; no dark theme exists.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean confirmed, pending and closed. They always appear as a dark tone on its own soft tint, never as a decorative accent.

rules.name: The White Workbench Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces are white. Material's green palette is overridden precisely so surfaces do not pick up a tint.

rules.name: The Heavy Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings and anything clickable are bold (700+). Regular weight is for reading text only.

rules.name: The One Arc Rule
rules.body: Red-to-gold means progress and nothing else. It is never a button, heading, border or decoration.

rules.name: The Whole Poster Rule
rules.body: Never crop the poster without setting what the crop removes as live text, and never add a second brand image beside it.

dos: Do style Material components through the global overrides in `styles.scss` so every screen stays consistent.
Do use `--card-shadow`, `--card-shadow-hover`, `--brand-grad`, `--tint-primary` and the `--mat-sys-*` tokens instead of new literals.
Do show registration state with `.status-pill` and its existing variants.
Do open each page with the page title pattern.
Do keep pills for buttons and tags, rounded rectangles for containers.
donts: Don't tint content surfaces; they are white by rule.
Don't use green, amber or red for decoration; they mean state.
Don't add square or sharp-cornered buttons.
Don't assume a dark theme; `color-scheme` is light only.
